exposure: Intrauterine transfusion (IUT) with fully phenotypically matched RBC units
outcome: Severity of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN)
Reduction in anti-D and anti-K titers
cohort: The study included five women with severe HDFN secondary to maternal red blood cell alloimmunization.
finding: A combined regimen of TPE and IVIG early in pregnancy followed by IUT later in pregnancy successfully managed severe maternal RBC alloimmunization and HDFN, resulting in the delivery of healthy infants.
